correctness.rationale: Off the all-left fixed face, inverse branches ((x−1)/2,y) and (y,(1−x)/2) contract both labels once the inverse word includes two right branches, so the square of any non-all-left word's inverse composition has a unique fixed point, also fixed by the composition. The closed branches do not introduce periodic switching points: if x_i denotes successive pre-right x values and ℓ_i the intervening left count, then x_(i−1)=1−(1+x_(i+1))/2^(ℓ_i+1), forcing all pre-right values below 1 and then strictly above 0. A left step from 0 would produce 1, also excluded. Thus the coded words count points, including smaller prime periods, not primitive orbits. At step j the doubled input label is 1 exactly for s_j=+1. At even parity the signed diagonal exponent difference is 1 plus n−1 free signs; the all-left word subtracts only the all-positive case. Odd parity gives anti-diagonal determinant 2^n and eigenvalues ±i 2^(n/2), hence equal moduli. The ordinary sign CLT, removal of one word, and the limiting parity weights give the stated folded mixture. Even n can have real-spectrum ties at finite n, and n=1 has no real-class conditioning; neither changes the limit. The supplied checker was inspected and not run; the all-n verification is analytic.
